subject: Evidence request: BYOK operator separation & cross-border subprocessor details (TechPulse)
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena@techpulse.io>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@techpulse.io
Date: Thu, 18 Sep 2025 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Evidence package for BYOK and operator separation (TechPulse)

Hi Irene,

Thanks for taking our call earlier. As part of TechPulse's security review for the private deployment (VPC) pilot we need an evidence package showing: 1) that customer-managed keys (BYOK) are enforced end-to-end and that Redwood operators do not have access to customer CMKs or plaintext data; 2) a current list of subprocessors with locations (we need to know any subprocessors that operate outside the EEA); and 3) a short description of how operator access is logged and how TechPulse can run/receive on-demand access audits.

Can you provide the artefacts below by COB Friday 24 Sep?
- Redacted architecture diagram highlighting cryptographic boundaries
- Signed attestation that operators cannot decrypt customer data under BYOK (one paragraph is fine)
- Current subprocessors CSV with country column
- Sample operator access audit log (schema or example)
- Any third-party audit/cert evidence relevant to this scope

Procurement may also ask for an amended DPA clause and an export-control statement — I cc'ed them to the thread. I can provide a PO if you want to attach your standard SOW.

Best,
Elena Morales
Director, Security & Compliance
TechPulse Inc.

P.S. Attaching our procurement checklist (TP_PO_903) for reference.

Irene — taking point on the technical pieces. Quick clarifications inline (forwarding Elena's original ask below for context).

Key points I'll include in the package:
- Cryptographic boundary: a small diagram showing where the CMK resides (customer KMS), how Redwood stores only wrapped keys/metadata, and how the runtime performs tokenization/attestation.
- Operator access: explicit statement that Redwood operators do not hold roots of trust for customer CMKs and cannot perform decryption without customer cooperation. We'll add the mechanism: customer CMK decrypts ephemeral session keys in the VPC at runtime; logs capture key-handshake events with nonce and request id.
- Escrow: we do not escrow customer CMKs as a default. If a customer requests an escrow arrangement for legal/continuity reasons we can propose an escrow workflow, but it requires a separate contract and notarized escrow events (rare).
- Subprocessors: the CSV Irene attached includes our primary infra and monitoring subprocessors. I'll flag any subprocessors operating in India and the US for cross-border considerations.

I'll prepare:
- A redacted sample audit log (single-session, minimal metadata)
- A one-paragraph signed attestation for the legal team to include in the DPA addendum
- A short runbook for on-demand audit requests and expected SLAs (48–72h initial response, deeper audit windows negotiated)

Laura — can you pull the sample log and the existing runbook draft? Happy to stitch together.
